paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's Word does its work when somebody actually hears it. The Book of the Law was found in the house of the LORD by Hilkiah the priest (2 Chronicles 34:14). The moment Josiah heard the words, he tore his clothes (2 Chronicles 34:19). A book on a shelf is just a book, but when a heart hears it and answers, things start to change.

Now look at how Josiah took it. The LORD says through Huldah, "because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words…" (2 Chronicles 34:27). He didn't argue with it, and he didn't shop around for a nicer version. I think a tender heart is the best oven mitt there is, because it lets you pick up hard words without dropping them. And the LORD says to him, "I have heard you" (2 Chronicles 34:27).

Then Josiah doesn't keep it to himself. He reads it to all the people, great and small, and makes a covenant to follow the LORD with all his heart and all his soul (2 Chronicles 34:30-31). So here's your takeaway, baker: open the Word, let it reach your heart, and then do what it says. Don't just nod at it like a recipe you'll totally try someday. And stay close, friend, because King Josiah's story isn't over.
